metadata.description: Opinionated Claude Code plugins for professional coding — language- and platform-specific authoring (rust-dev, android-dev, browser-extensions, game-dev, i18n), cross-cutting dev workflow (git-github, release-promo, infra-build, loadout; planning redirects to staged-planning), each with a deterministic validation lane where applicable. The AI-tool-authoring family (plugin-dev + six platform siblings) now lives in the sibling agent-tooling marketplace.

plugins.name: rust-dev
plugins.description: Idiomatic Rust authoring: a rust-coding progressive-disclosure knowledge-router skill and a rust-expert authoring subagent, sharing one plugin-level references/ set. rust-expert covers author/review/idiomize/audit/migrate via protocols plus review, idiomize, and project-audit modes.

plugins.name: android-dev
plugins.description: Android development plugin: Gradle build management, a per-stage on-device verify gate (build the debug APK, detect an adb device, install + smoke-launch + run instrumented tests), UI/UX design with Material 3 and Figma including a screenshot-grading evaluator loop (emulator captures scored against a weighted design rubric by a separate evaluator), multi-device emulator orchestration via MCP, mock server generation from app sources, automated screenshot capture across phone and tablet form factors, release signing, and end-to-end publishing flows for F-Droid and Google Play.

plugins.name: release-promo
plugins.description: Drafts release-announcement posts for the platforms a project actually belongs on. Skills for Reddit (with explicit guidance for Matrix subs r/matrixprotocol and r/matrixdotorg, plus language and topic subs), This Week in Matrix, Hacker News Show HN, Lobsters, and Fediverse. The /promote-release command surveys the repo, picks eligible channels, and drafts one post per channel.

plugins.name: infra-build
plugins.description: Make a project buildable by the three publishing pipelines under ~/dev/infra: utils (Debian .deb via pkgskel + reprepro), build-for-mac (Rust → macOS .pkg via GitHub Actions), and publish-images (multi-arch Docker → DockerHub/GHCR/Quay/GitLab/ECR). Skills audit readiness, scaffold the missing file layout, and register the project in both the data file and the workflow YAML in lockstep so the two never drift. A deterministic validation lane (scripts/validate.sh → validate-deb.sh + validate-readiness.sh, on a shared JSON finding contract) owns the mechanical deb-tree and source-repo checks; the skills add the cross-repo registration-sync judgment.

plugins.name: git-github
plugins.description: Everyday git/GitHub operations for Claude Code: run a single-tool authoritative code review via the bundled read-only code-reviewer agent (also consumed by planning's executing-plans for per-task and per-stage review), audit a repo or diff for faked verification — stubbed gate tasks, tests that never ran, fabricated evidence, hidden exclusions — via gate-audit (the after-the-fact enforcement of planning's honest-gates rules), dispatch the same diff to sibling CLIs (codex/gemini/opencode) for multi-model second opinions, audit code comments for explanatory value, audit GitHub Actions workflows for errors and outdated actions, sweep every portfolio project's GitHub repo for red default-branch workflows, unaddressed issues, stale PRs, and open Dependabot alerts via a deterministic gh-CLI scanner and triage picked findings into per-project backlogs (repo-health), review and tighten READMEs, audit dependency licenses and pick a project LICENSE, and cut release tags. The GitHub Actions workflow lane also emits findings on plugin-dev's shared deterministic contract via scripts/validate.sh. Skills auto-trigger on natural language; nothing autoposts, force-pushes, or rewrites history.

plugins.name: planning
plugins.description: Redirect: planning now lives in sureserverman/staged-planning, and this entry installs it from there (plugins/claude/planning). Staged, gate-checked plans: brainstorm a design, write a plan whose stages end in runnable checks, execute it Red-Green with honest gates and code review, keep a backlog and decisions. The portfolio and compass skills moved to vault-portfolio@obsidian-wiki. Install this entry or planning@staged-planning, not both: with both enabled, every planning hook runs twice.

plugins.name: business
plugins.description: Per-project business-planning pipeline for the ~/dev portfolio: turn a shippable project into a commercial decision and keep it tracked. assess runs a viability triage (repo + vault + MATURITY.md context, a questions-first interview that confirms inferred audience/substitutes/willingness-to-pay rather than assuming them, opt-in --research that reuses any fresh market-research.md or dispatches the cited market-researcher subagent at triage depth) and writes a schema-versioned business/BUSINESS.md with a verdict (monetize | free-for-reputation | internal-only | park), target audience, and evidence tag; revenue-model turns an assess-passed verdict into a monetization decision (model, pricing hypothesis, channels, numeric dated targets) one choice at a time; market-research runs a standalone cited competitive analysis at an operator-selected depth tier (brief | standard | deep) following a working method — a competitor is anyone who solves the same problem, listed in three passes (category, customer-job, alternatives) with a rate-based coverage threshold, priced, channelled, and at standard/deep built into a competitor table (business/competitor-table.yaml, four characteristic categories, every cell a quantity) that the deterministic competitor-table.py normalizes to a −5…+5 scale, sweeps for the axis pair where the project differs from everyone, and renders as quadrant and trajectory SVGs, plus six-block competitor profiles, a per-competitor marketing teardown, a durability-of-advantage test, a five-component positioning, partner candidates, battlecards, monitoring indicators, and customer personas — persisted to a schema-3 business/market-research.md (with competitors row count and coverage exhausted|open) for assess and business-plan to reuse; business-plan composes the verdict, monetization, market research, gtm, and metrics plus a questions-first gap interview into a tiered twelve-section schema-2 business/plan.md (executive summary, problem & solution, customer personas, market analysis, competitive landscape, SWOT & positioning, product & roadmap, marketing & sales, operations, financial scenarios, risks, milestones), reusing research only at effective depth standard+ and offering missing prerequisites instead of fabricating them; launch produces a go-to-market plan at business/gtm-plan.md in the house checklist format (portfolio-unify-parseable so its progress rolls up like any plan), guarded by the project's MATURITY.md state so it warns before planning a launch for something far from ship-ready; track records actuals into an append-only business/metrics.md (free GitHub metrics auto-collected via collect-github.py, revenue/installs and an optional marketing funnel entered manually), diffs them against targets, and bumps the Last reviewed stamp; biz-portfolio sweeps every registry project via the deterministic business-scan.py evidence lane (the SOLE parser of the business artifacts — BUSINESS.md, market-research.md, plan.md, gtm-plan.md, metrics.md, with per-artifact schema ceilings and depth/coverage validation — one JSON contract, reusing staged-planning's lib/plan_parser.py regexes for gtm progress) and rebuilds the global-business.md roll-up, flagging research/plans older than 90 days as STALE. A determinism boundary keeps all parsing in business-scan.py so vault-portfolio's portfolio and compass skills consume its JSON additively (including research/plan staleness) and degrade loudly when the business plugin is absent.

plugins.name: browser-extensions
plugins.description: Authoring and shipping browser extensions (WebExtensions) for Chrome, Firefox, and Firefox for Android. Skill `browser-extensions` covers manifest v3 migration, content scripts, permissions, store rejections, and the Firefox-for-Android caveats. Skill `amo-compliance-check` runs a preflight audit (manifest, permissions justification, minified-source rules, addon ID) before submission to addons.mozilla.org and ships a `scripts/amo-check.py` linter. The mechanical AMO checks also emit findings on the plugin-dev shared JSON contract via `scripts/validate.sh` (the `validate-amo.sh` lane).

plugins.name: loadout
plugins.description: Per-project plus per-task plugin loadouts. Layers a sticky tech baseline (android/rust/web-ext/...) with on-demand task overlays (security-audit/release/wiki/...) and writes the resulting `enabledPlugins` map to .claude/settings.local.json so only the plugins relevant to the current work load at session start. Detects the tech baseline automatically from Cargo.toml / build.gradle / manifest.json on first entry; task overlays toggle via /loadout +name and /loadout -name.

plugins.name: i18n
plugins.description: Internationalization (i18n) for any project that has user-facing strings. Skill `i18n-audit` detects the project's i18n framework (gettext .po, i18next JSON, Vue i18n, react-intl/FormatJS, Android strings.xml, iOS .strings/.stringsdict, Flutter ARB, Rails YAML, Django .po, Qt .ts, .NET .resx, Java .properties) and runs three Python scripts: detect-framework.py, scan-hardcoded.py (heuristic finder for likely user-facing strings still in source), and diff-catalogs.py (missing/stale-key gap analysis across locales). Skill `i18n-translate` drives an LLM translation pass that preserves placeholders (printf, ICU MessageFormat, {{handlebars}}, %1$s positional, Android XML quoting) and CLDR plural categories; ships validate-placeholders.py and extract-missing.py. Skill `i18n-formats` documents per-format gotchas. Sonnet-pinned translator subagent does the actual locale fills. A shared-contract validation lane (scripts/validate.sh, vendored from the plugin-dev determinism kit) wraps the catalog-diff and placeholder/CLDR-plural Python and emits findings on the common plugin-dev JSON contract. The three skills are invocable directly (`/i18n:i18n-audit`, `/i18n:i18n-translate`, `/i18n:i18n-formats`).

plugins.name: game-dev
plugins.description: Designs and reviews game mechanics, game feel, camera/navigation, UX/FTUE, accessibility, and code architecture for Godot 4, Unity 6, and Unreal 5. Every rule cites the source it came from — Schell, Sylvester, Swink, Nystrom, Hodent, Nesky's 50 Camera Mistakes, and the Game Accessibility Guidelines. Use /game-review for a scoped diff review (mechanics + feel + camera + UX + a11y + architecture) that plays a runnable build before grading feel/UX and labels findings reviewed-live vs static-only, and /game-mechanic for a guided mechanic-design session that outputs an implementable brief. Sonnet-pinned game-design-expert subagent handles all dispatches; nothing is auto-applied.
